content.text: {"persuasion":"PERSUADED","support_scope":"FULL","rationale":"The BOOK ENTRY's core identification — east as 'the front,' the quarter of beginnings and returns, grounded in the Hebrew qedem uniting 'east,' 'before,' and 'ancient' — is a lexically verifiable claim (qedem/qedmah does carry all three senses in biblical Hebrew, e.g., Gen 2:8 miqqedem; Deut 33:27 'the eternal God' elohei qedem) and every assertion actually printed in the entry is carried by its cited texts. Gen 2:8 places Eden eastward; Ex 27:13-16 places the tabernacle court's single gate on the east side, making the east literally the sanctuary's front door; Ezek 43:1-4 shows the glory of the LORD returning into the house 'by the way of the gate whose prospect is toward the east'; Ezek 46:1-3 shows the east gate as the ceremonial front where prince and people worship; Matt 24:27 has the coming of the Son of Man move from east to west. The entry's 'front' framing is not a rival to the common interpretation (direction of God's glory, presence, and Christ's coming) but an explanatory deepening of the same referent: it explains WHY the glory and the coming arrive from the east (it is the front/entrance quarter) and simultaneously accounts for the negative Genesis strand (expulsion eastward is expulsion out the front entrance, with cherubim posted at the east of the garden as at a doorway — mirrored by the cherubim-guarded sanctuary veil). The strongest genuine rival — Response B's primary reading that east fundamentally means exile, separation, and judgment — cannot explain the entry's cited architectural and theophanic texts: if east symbolized alienation, the sanctuary would not open eastward, the glory would not re-enter through the east gate, and the Son of Man's coming would not run east to west. That counter also cannot explain the qedem lexical facts. No supplied text defeats any printed assertion, so support is FULL and the verdict is PERSUADED.","book_core_identification":"East is 'the front' — the quarter of beginnings and of returns — because Hebrew qedem simultaneously means 'east,' 'before/in front,' and 'ancient': Eden is planted there, the sanctuary's entrance faces it, God's glory returns through it, and Christ's coming proceeds from it, with the literal compass direction serving as the image beneath the symbol.","book_secondary_elaborations":["Eden is planted eastward (Gen 2:8)","The sanctuary's front door/court gate is on the east (Ex 27:13-16; Ezek 46:1-3)","God's glory returns through the east gate (Ezek 43:1-4)","Christ's coming moves from east to west (Matt 24:27)","The compass direction is the literal image beneath the symbol","Opposite: West (the 'hinder' quarter)"],"unsupported_glossary_assertions":[],"chapter_only_objections":["The chapter's identification of Babylon the Great as Jerusalem riding a western seven-mountain bloc, and 'hindermost of the nations' (Jer 50:12) as meaning westernmost, are contested typological applications not asserted in the glossary entry.","The chapter's claim that the 'hinder sea' word-family (Deut 11:24; Zech 14:8) proves a full east-front/west-behind compass system is used in the entry only implicitly via 'Opposite: West'; the geopolitical inferences built on it are chapter-level claims.","The Exodus-as-similitude-of-the-Fall-of-Babylon parallel, the rod/serpent/tail derivations, and the north-as-lurker's-quarter argument are outside the entry's scope."],"strongest_counter_interpretation":"East primarily symbolizes exile, separation from God's presence, and judgment (Response B): eastward movement in Genesis marks departure from Eden and escalating rebellion (Gen 3:24; 4:16; 11:2; 13:11), and the east wind is God's instrument of destruction (Ex 10:13; Hos 13:15; Jon 4:8), making the positive glory/advent texts a secondary, later strand.","counter_core_identification":"East is the direction of departure from God — exile, alienation, and incoming judgment — rather than the front from which divine beginnings and returns proceed.","counter_relation_to_book_core":"CONTRADICTS","material_core_denial":"The counter denies that east is the sanctuary-front quarter of divine arrival and return, asserting instead that east is intrinsically the quarter of estrangement and judgment; both cannot be the governing core of the same symbol.","counter_case":["Genesis's post-fall geography consistently sends the estranged eastward: cherubim east of Eden (Gen 3:24), Cain to Nod east of Eden (Gen 4:16), Babel's builders eastward to Shinar (Gen 11:2), Lot east toward Sodom (Gen 13:11).","The east wind is repeatedly God's scourge: blasted grain (Gen 41:6), locusts (Ex 10:13), scattering (Jer 18:17), desolation (Hos 13:15), affliction (Jon 4:8).","Invaders and corrupting influences come from the east: Midianites and the people of the east (Judg 6:3), diviners from the east (Isa 2:6).","On this reading, the positive advent texts are a distinct prophetic reversal motif, not the base meaning."],"book_explanatory_advantages":["The qedem lexical bridge (east = front = ancient) is hard linguistic data that only the book's reading uses; it explains why the same word denotes direction, position, and primeval time.","It explains the sanctuary architecture: the tabernacle court gate (Ex 27:13-16), the priestly camp of Moses and Aaron eastward (cf. Num 3:38), and Ezekiel's east gate all face east because east is the front — the counter has no account of why holy space opens toward the supposed quarter of alienation.","It explains both valences with one mechanism: glory enters by the front (Ezek 43:1-4) and the expelled exit by the front (Gen 3:24, cherubim stationed at the east of the garden exactly as at a sanctuary entrance), so exile-eastward is a special case of the front-door image rather than a contradiction.","It explains the vector of Matt 24:27 — the coming proceeds from east to west because arrival comes through the front.","It explains Ezek 46:1-3, where prince and people worship at the east gate 'before the LORD' — worship happens at the front."],"counter_explanatory_advantages":["The counter foregrounds the Genesis exile pattern and the east-wind judgment texts as a coherent literary motif, which the entry does not explicitly mention.","It accounts for hostile 'people of the east' texts without needing the front-door frame."],"evidence_book_core_cannot_explain":[],"comparative_winner":"BOOK","decisive_sources":["Genesis 2:8 (garden planted eastward/miqqedem)","Exodus 27:13-16 (the court's only gate on the east side — the sanctuary's front)","Ezekiel 43:1-4 (the glory of the God of Israel returns 'from the way of the east' through the east-facing gate)","Ezekiel 46:1-3 (prince and people worship at the east gate before the LORD)","Matthew 24:27 (the coming of the Son of Man from east to west)"],"unresolved_objections":["The entry does not itself address the negative east-motifs (eastward exile, east wind judgment), though its front-door frame can absorb them; a fuller entry would note the dual valence flagged by all four common-interpretation responses.","The 'Opposite: West' marker rests on the hinder-sea word-family argument made only in the chapter, though it follows naturally from qedem = front."],"confidence":"high"}
